title: Librarian, or librarian with a book club?
hook: Two stories about Sam. Which one is more likely to be true?

knows: probability as a share of cases
doesNotKnow: that 'A and B' can never be more likely than 'A', however well B fits the description

misconception: A detail that fits the description makes the fuller story more likely (Sam, quiet and bookish, is more likely a librarian who runs a book club than just a librarian).
objective: The learner can explain that 'librarian who runs a book club' is a subset of 'librarian', so it can never be more likely, however well the extra detail fits.

claims.text: Every librarian who runs a book club is a librarian, so the people who are both are a subset of the librarians: P(A and B) <= P(A), equal only if every librarian runs a club. Each added detail can only remove people, so a more specific story is never more likely.
claims.source: P(A and B) = P(A) P(B | A) and P(B | A) <= 1. On the stage the inner ring is built from the first clubbers(lib, club) dots of the librarians (model.ts), so inner <= outer for every slider setting; the club slider stops at 90%. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. P(A and B) = P(A)P(B|A) <= P(A). Own check of model.ts over every slider setting (lib 5..50 step 5, club 10..90 step 20): inner < outer in all 50, since the club slider stops at 90%.

claims.text: The stage's town (1,000 people who fit Sam's description) and its shares are a model chosen for the card, not data about librarians.
claims.source: Lesson rule (brief Round 3 item 3, planned claim 2). model.ts: librarians = round(1000 * lib%), clubbers = round(librarians * club%); lib 5-50%, club 10-90%. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. model.ts: librarians = round(1000 lib%), clubbers = round(librarians club%); header states the shares are a model chosen for the card.

claims.text: The reveal quotes the current club share and the dots in each ring, and the counts recorded when the club share reached 90% (e.g. 180 of 200 at 20% librarians on the QA path).
claims.source: Demo.tsx reveal and note(); model.ts librarians(20) = 200, clubbers(20, 90) = 180; librarians(10) = 100, clubbers(10, 90) = 90 (the brief's check). | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own: librarians(20) = 200, clubbers(20, 90) = 180; librarians(10) = 100, clubbers(10, 90) = 90. Reveal quotes current club share and rings, plus the record at 90% only when it differs from the current state.

claims.text: (Not shown to the learner.) Ranking a conjunction above one of its parts is called the conjunction fallacy; in the 'Linda' problem most respondents made it.

recall.question: Alex is outgoing and loves numbers. Which is more likely: Alex is an accountant, or Alex is an accountant who plays poker?
options: Alex is an accountant who plays poker
recall.why: Every accountant who plays poker is an accountant, so the fuller story is a subset: it can feel more fitting but can never be more likely.
